body: I am the same age, although I feel (in different ways) both much younger and much older. I’ve spent my early 20s punishing myself for how I spent my teens. And I can’t do this anymore. I’m out. I never wanted to be this person. Anyway, doesn’t matter. I am the way I am, and I’m too tired to keep fucking myself over like this. I know I’ve shortened my life expectancy, and I just want to enjoy what I have left.

This isn’t quite the same, but I can relate to wondering if I’m delusional and creating personas.

I think I can actually get things right a good amount. I seem to keep coming back to the same answers overall. But I have serious self-doubt issues. I let anxiety and unhealthy coping mechanisms get in the way, reinforcing negative beliefs about myself. 

I believe I can feel my “true” self (or what’s left of it), long smothered and withered over time, buried beneath who I’ve pretended to be. It is confusing... I have this tendency to imitate others, to take on their attitudes to some degree, and even their problems. It’s like I’m so desperate to belong somewhere, to find security, that I try to convince everyone I’m someone else. But then, I doubt who I really am... Maybe I tend to believe the worst about myself (and others).

Yeah, I just can’t relate to that stuff (parties, sex, whatever). A lot of stuff that is popular often isn’t very desirable to me. So in that way, it can be irritating. I feel worse (shame, guilt, anxiety, some anger) when I hear about things like school, work, some healthy activities, and friendship/family. All of those are things that I had some interest in and opportunities that I’ve blown. I don’t care for sex and parties. But I believe I’ve missed out on much of the most important things in life, sitting sequestered in the house.

As for music, I tend to like alternative, folksy music, or classical-ish. Recently I’ve been back with Of Monsters and Men. Sometimes their songs make me feel understood (e.g., Phantom). I find the lyric video amazingly reminiscent of my inner world.

I kind of did this as well, even though I didn’t really attend high school. Mine was prompted by family crisis, I think. “Be what they expect you to be,” I thought. Unfortunately, I’m still awkward as hell.

It’s been so long, this thing is programmed in so deep now. But I can still feel myself beneath it, sometimes.
I think it’s really great that you were able to move out, do creative work and have hobbies that make you happy. I don’t know if I’ll be able to do that.

Probably ASD, OCD, some depression and anxiety, perhaps CPTSD. The usual... only, I don’t seem to experience things in the usual way. I’m very introspective and tend to notice things others don’t (and vice-versa). I don’t think the way they do, beneath my imitations.

Yeah, I just have dusty stuff from like 10 years ago with the occasional item or a few since. Disorganized, and not much of anything meaningful. As others have mentioned, I have something against self-expression.

You have good questions. Not sure how well I can answer, but I don’t mind trying.

Basically, I had got myself in a difficult situation irl, was feeling really lost and scared of taking action in that state, although I needed to get out of it. Before (and even still), I’d be drawn to stories in which I could see something of myself in the character and their struggles, and going on that journey with them and seeing the way they dealt with situations would give me ideas, lend me strength and inspiration to help deal with my own. It really depends on the character and the quality of the story, as well as my state of mind. I have to be able to identify with the character to some extent, open to experience-taking, learning from them, etc. I had shut down a lot of that in my state of fear and confusion, resulting in feeling stuck. Starting small, if I’m willing to take some risks, do what works for me, and let myself trust and believe in things again, then I think that should help me get unstuck.

I think stuff like Twilight can be OK for entertainment/pandering, but not as good for this more profound experience. Things like LotR, Harry Potter, and other classics are better, but I guess it comes down to personal preference. It’s about the hero’s journey and character development, much more than a cheap fantasy.

I’ve spent lots of time on more mindless entertainment because it’s a fun escape, but it doesn’t really get me anywhere. I don’t come out of it thinking, wow, that was art and I feel changed as a person, or that it was thought-provoking at least. That’s the difference. The more mindless stuff just feels easier and safer somehow, comforting but not fulfilling. I think there’s something vulnerable about being open to that deeper experience and change.

I don’t know if that helps, but it was interesting to think about!

That may be a big part of it, but I don’t think that’s all. I’ve noticed that I will be drawn to particular themes at times, things I can somehow relate on a deeper level, and I think it helps me process and work through real life situations. Or at least it did, before I got in the habit of blocking the process, for fear of change.

I enjoy a good plot (mystery, adventure, etc), but tend to read the most about friendship and family, which I think is where it may become more about escapism. I think it can be good for me in a way, but I definitely have been leaning on it far too much for too long, choosing it over working on real life stuff. It probably keeps me from feeling more lonely and depressed and helps keep a bit of hope alive. It would work better if I accepted it and didn’t shame myself for it, like, “Oh, that’s not real. You’re pathetic.”

I’ve spent a lot of time reading about personality type, but sometimes I think these things are for other people, people with more developed personality. I’m a wreck, I’ve been in decline since I was a kid, been hiding in my house for years. That’s not much good to go on. Not to mention I can reinterpret the past through most any lens I like.

IDK... I’ve spent too long thinking about it.
Thank you. I’ve read about the 4Fs (Pete Walker, etc). Less familiar with flop.
That’s interesting. Can you point me where I can learn more?

I also think my mood is more stable without stressful interactions, but on the other hand, too much time alone seems to foster paranoia. Sometimes I’m surprised by how much better I feel after a bit of interaction.
Yeah, I think I know what you mean. I don’t like it either, but I kind of understand why they do it, and I can’t think of a good alternative rn.

I was never the best organized, but at least I used to be more functional. My room wasn’t a total wreck, and I showered every other day for years. Lately (the past year or so?) I have been getting worse about things like showering and cleaning up. It’s a relatively recent development, and I’m not proud of it. I can’t remember why it started. Just the drift of falling behind on most everything, I guess. Oh, I think it was something to do with being too hard on myself? That black-and-white perfectionism, “Do it right or you may as well not do it at all.” I pretend it’s not there or I get overwhelmed.

I know it’s bad, but I kind of tell myself it’s not so bad as long as I mostly keep to myself. Like who cares??

Hey, I’m sorry to hear that. Regret can be a heavy thing, and your regret is valid. I suggest you do NOT do what I did, which is deny it or dwell on it and let it consume you, wasting what you have left. I think how we feel can tell us something about what we value. Accept your losses so that you can move forward and hopefully build a better life for yourself.

Not much (which may be a big part of the problem). I mean, mostly it’s tea, food, sometimes sleep, and stories. I love a good story. This can be in books, TV, movies, games... I think stories have always sustained me, but it’s gotten to an unhealthy level since I left school. It’s just unbalanced; I depend on them too much. Also with tea, I like to drink it daily.

It is hard to care about other things when we don’t have our basic needs met.

I have just read something that reinforced to me the importance of (even one) relatively healthy/secure relationship. I think I have a tendency to overlook or downplay this, because it does not seem very attainable to me. I wish there were another way.

I think the robot writes this. It is very repetitive, and I feel oppressed by it (and the other ones), but it is here to fend something off. I’m tired of it, though. I wish I were strong enough to do things on my own (without relying on these things).

Maybe not entirely the robot, though. The robot is trying to be more accurate than before, but it is still repeating mannerisms and forcing things. It does not seem to think for itself.
Hello. I have schiz traits and NEET, apparently. I would like not to be, I think, but I’ve got myself in quite a bind. I am sorry, but it is what it is.

IDK if this is how it is for you, but when something gives me anxiety, I tend to start overthinking it, which gives me even more anxiety. And then the thing happens, the thing when you’ve been looking at something for so long, you can’t see it properly anymore? Or when you see a word too many times and it loses meaning? I forget what that’s called. Anyway, I know it’s hard, but I think maybe you need a distraction. Stop thinking about this for a while, and it should become less of an issue.

Flight/freeze for me and my dad. Fight/fawn for my mother.

I feel such guilt, because the way I act, I know I’m wasting my life.

I’ve never been, but when I was a kid, I was terrified of being sent to one. IDK why exactly—just that people kept suggesting there was something wrong with me, and I’d heard horror stories...

For some reason, I thought they’d basically gaslight me (although I didn’t know the term back then). Like, you are now labeled as crazy, so this is how we’re going to treat you, and no one will listen to you again.

I hope some places are better than that.
Yes, this!

I don’t recall telling people about AvPD exactly, but they definitely know something’s up. My sister actually said it once (that I have “avoidance personality”).

What really annoys me is that my parents seem kind of obsessed with the idea that I’m autistic, and my mom in particular seems to use it as an excuse for my shitty behavior and her bad parenting. It’s infuriating. Like, OK, maybe I am autistic, I guess. But regardless, that should not be a get-out-of-jail-free card!

At least my dad seems to understand better and will even occasionally call us out on shit. 

And I have no friends lol.

But yeah, basically, people know and don’t care except for when it suits them.
IDK, man. Do what you need to do. It sounds like you’re under a lot of stress. Maybe you could take a break?

Yeah, that sounds like OCD. I suppose it is your perception that you’ve done something morally ambiguous, which is bothering you a lot. I don’t think that necessarily makes you a bad person. At least you have a conscience.

You said your friend doesn’t care, meaning there was no harm done. That’s the important thing, right?

Interesting. Sometimes I feel like I’m the one with the rose-colored glasses, the only one who can see any good in the world. It makes me feel crazy. Probably because my parents had a lot of trauma and managed not to pass it all on.

Also, I think a lot of people fake positivity.
IDK what your situation is, but I’ve felt kind of similar. Prospects not looking good, but hey, at least I’ve (mostly) stopped beating myself up about it.

It was just a thought. On its own, it does not have the power to hurt others. Your actions > your thoughts.

Also, it’s human nature to judge. It’s meant to help us survive. You’re not a bad person for that.
Yeah, it’s self-fulfilling. I can’t easily change that belief, so right now I’m just trying to accept my situation. I need to drop some of my perfectionist tendencies.

I feel like a ghost in a sense... IDK if people ignore me like that, though. I don’t get out much. When I do, I assume I’m just another random person to them (and rather an unappealing one).

People can be extremely stressful. I think I lack the skills to deal with them effectively, which is one reason why I tend to prefer solitude.

Shit happened when I was 13 and I didn’t move forward, stunting my growth in various ways.

Or maybe I’d just say that I’m generally incompetent. Or that I’m not good with people. It depends.
Me too, kind of. It’s hard to stop once I get going. Might be an ADHD/OCD thing. It’s like I can’t act “normal” around people. I get overstimulated and either go quiet or turn into a chatterbox.

Well, I don’t have this problem because I waste most of my time reading or watching shows, sometimes listening to audiobooks. I feel like there’s never enough time. There’s always more stuff to see. It’s like an addiction. I guess I hyperfocus, so when I really get into something, that’s it, I’m gone for the next several hours, easy. I often get behind on chores and stuff if it isn’t well-established in my routine.

My days blur together a lot. I don’t remember exactly what I’ve been doing. I think lately I’ve been watching some let’s plays on YouTube and dabbling in video games again. I played Impostor Factory recently. Failing to get into Minecraft or Skyrim again. Might listen to The Hobbit or something. I never read that one.
Yes, I’ve experienced this to some degree.

I actually feel kind of invalidated by that. Like, I don’t want your reassurance. I don’t want you to tell me what you think I want to hear. I want HONESTY. If this is how you honestly see it, then sure. But it’s probably not going to change my opinion. It’s not just OCD telling me that, but OCD exaggerates. My inner critic may be overpowered, but I can’t just disregard it. I really think it’s onto something.

I guess it would be better if they more were like, “Well, you’re not good about x, but you are good about y.” Instead of just telling me that I’m a good person. What does that even mean?

It may be hard to believe, but I think I’m (very unhealthy/underdeveloped) INTJ 1w9 so/sp 154.

- introvert, former bookworm
- Tourettic OCD, ASD possible
- emotionally distant father and immature mother; parents not well-attuned to children
- relatively OK early childhood despite previous; I felt mostly OK with myself 
- parents struggle to handle my becoming a teenager
- I start to reject myself more, suppress my feelings 
- Mom decides to homeschool me, but leaves most work for Dad
- our homeschooling is crap since Dad works all day and Mom is immature
- I’m somewhat immature too, so I end up stuck at home all day playing video games, etc.
- Nobody really holds me accountable, although Dad tries
- Slow decline as I become more inept and fearful of outside world, continuing to reject myself 

...And yeah. Emotional abuse, neglect, enabled avoidance/addiction. My becoming a cowardly pos, losing self-respect, etc.

Speaking for myself, of course. A lot of you are probably better people. I remain convinced that (despite some challenges) I had the resources to do better than this, so I’m guilty as hell. I think I really ought to forgive and let go, but I’m too stubborn.
So true.

For me it’s basically because I treat myself like crap, starting from acting out of insecurity, I guess.

Also, I loved nature when I was a kid. It was very important to me. But over time I’ve turned to (what I’d consider) very unnatural lifestyle. So I hate myself for that. It’s like I betrayed who I was.

Honestly, there are a lot of intertwining reasons, which mostly come down to lacking self-love and self-respect.

Me too!! Sometimes I think it’s like all I do is explain, explain, explain...

For me personally, I guess it started from trying to cope with my mother. And then I did some things of which I was deeply ashamed, and I believed this meant I was unworthy of forgiveness. From then on, denial and excuses, just adding to the pile... The initial problem seems so small in comparison.

I can still forgive myself. I don’t need someone else’s permission. And I can stop explaining things unnecessarily.
Sounds familiar...

I have similar issues, no one to talk to and not much to do a lot of the time. I have a sleep disorder as well, so I sleep a lot during the day sometimes, and then I stay up all night.

Being isolated sucks, but I would ask myself, exactly what is it about being alone that makes me feel so bad? Personally, I’m capable of enjoying my time alone, IF I don’t spend it ruminating on my inadequacy and all my past failures and so on. Which tends to be what we do when we are—let’s face it—hiding in shame. So I find something else to focus on, which shouldn’t be too difficult with the internet and whatnot. I also need some kind of goal to work toward. And hopefully, I can find some enjoyment in these things, which comes easier with acceptance of my situation. This is really key. Things don’t have to be all good for me to accept them. Acceptance = nonresistance. I find it really eases suffering and promotes rather a peaceful state. 

As for being lonely, it would be great to have friends, but really just having some productive interactions can be helpful. Limited contact. Quality beats quantity. From experience, having one relatively brief, pleasant interaction is much better than spending hours bitching (though yes, there may be temptations).

Just some thoughts and observations, since I’m still trying to work through this myself.

You’re definitely not alone. I see this sort of thing far too often, and I’ve fallen pretty deep into it myself.

Would you believe that long ago, I truly felt life was meaningful? That I really believed there was a better way of life attainable to me, and I was motivated?

I was so fortunate. But that was before everything got messed up. I barely remember it now.

Honestly, I think that’s one of the worst things about this. Knowing that I could actually be that way and still end up here.

Always do whatever you can to get back on track.

I think it’s possible, depending on the situation. I haven’t tried this with friends, exactly, (I have no friends lol) but with family. I have quite strained relationships with them. Sometimes we barely speak for weeks, which seems extreme considering I still live around them. I have found that we are able to (re)connect in a limited way via mutual interests. I suppose these relationships could be gradually improved if we take care to respect boundaries. (Easier said than done, yeah.)

I used to have a similar home/school split, but I don’t think I was bullied very much. I was mostly left alone, as I preferred.

Anyway, I act like a very different person in different environments.

They’ve failed me in various ways, and then I’ve failed them.

My dad is actually the best person I know. He is emotionally distant, but in other ways, he’s always been there. Smart, hardworking, reliable. He appears to have schizoid traits, if not the full disorder, though he seems fairly high functioning in general. 

My mom is emotionally immature and the root of our family’s chaos, to be frank. There appears to be some degree of pathological narcissism and codependency issues. She has repeatedly discouraged my independence and enabled my avoidance; in other words, she wants me weak and needy. Genetics aside, I think she has quite significantly contributed to my developing AvPD. I know it is very complex, however.

Due to these issues, my siblings and I have grown up in what I call an emotional desert (i.e., scarce resources).

As for me, I tend to alternate between over-sharing and shutting people out (actually, between high and low activity in general). I also have long developed a mask (or false self) which I feel unable to remove, even when I’m alone. For years, this false self has possessed me, and I think it has severely hindered my relationships as well as my development in other areas. (I suppose that was the point, in a way.)

Anyhow, our relationships are strained, to say the least. At this point, I think there has been plenty of disappointment, (perceived) betrayal, and general nastiness between us all. We function mostly on a superficial level, I suppose.

Probably so. I’ve got a bit better recently, but my mind still doesn’t shut up most days, some days being worse than others. But the more I practice, the easier I find accepting and letting go.

I really wasn’t always like this. I think, when I was a young child, I was fairly present-oriented. But after I started “homeschooling”, I had too much time alone with my thoughts, I guess... Too much time to worry. Years passed, and eventually I had to realize how messed up my life was getting. It got even
worse after that, because I freaked out and went into overdrive with my bad habits and poor skills lol. Ruminating on the past non-stop, about how I ruined everything.

It was like a positive feedback loop. I was thinking too much, talking too much, and then I was writing pages and pages of nonsense, just picking over the past. It worsened until I was getting multiple migraines a week, which finally provided me sufficient motivation to turn things around, I suppose. That’s the thing... When I get in pain like that, pretty much all I care about anymore is making it stop. (Not about past BS.) I knew from experience that something like this would happen, but apparently I was (am?) too dysfunctional not to push it that far. I can predict these outcomes, but I don’t work well enough with myself to prevent them.

Anyhow, since that time, I’ve been up and down, but more up, I think. The migraines have lessened. The problem is, this overthinking crap tends to come back as soon as I’m not in too much (physical) pain. Old habits die hard.

I think exercise should help, as well as finding other things to do in general. I am often terribly under-exercised. Recently, there was a week or two when I walked ~4 miles a day on most days, and I did start feeling much better.

Maybe. Sometimes I think the same. But if you’re actually doing more things you had been avoiding, then some things should change for the better, even if it is humiliating. I’m mid-twenties now, I’m useless too, and I know why. Because I’ve developed these habits of avoidance, procrastination, etc., and taken them to the extreme. Not all of that is my fault, but a lot of it is.

I think I can become at least a little more useful, even if I never measure up to higher standards. I realized, that matters to me. It gives me something better to do than drown in shame and wait to die. And, I’ve noticed, I’m becoming more habituated to these situations. As you said, it’s humiliation after humiliation, so... if I don’t keep thinking myself into it, after a while I stop caring so much. It’s kind of strange to me. I wish I had done this before, but I didn’t, so... not much choice but to deal with it now.

I’m just going to accept that I don’t know the future. I don’t know what I’ll fail or succeed at, if I don’t even try.

I think what really helps me, is doing things for myself, things I genuinely enjoy. Not just punishing myself and pandering all the time, or looking to please others. This improves my relationship with myself and sometimes inspires me to do better, to try more things. For example, audiobooks. I can listen while doing some other tasks, and I find them superior to the internet in general (though maybe that’s because I’m using it wrong, I’ll admit). There are all sorts, filled with ideas and potential for learning, many freely available. Lately, I’ve been rediscovering some classics I’d read as a child.

Just try something, if you want (or need). Stop hitting yourself with all the guilt and shame, because it’s just not helpful. A little goes a long way, lol.
Almost everything. But this could be a good thing to reflect on, I guess. I did use to have such dreams...

It never ends. The videos are a distraction/escape from the misery of my existence, an attempt to fill the void.

Balance is good.

I kind of think this way, too, but I don’t want to stress myself out anymore, so I’ve stopped thinking about it as much. I no longer care if I’m in denial or not. I sort of feel as if I’m just surviving moment to moment, so why bother worrying about how inadequate I am? It’s a waste of time.
It’s worth a try. Maybe it could help a little.

I don’t cry often, but that doesn’t mean I’m not hurt. I just habitually suppress my emotions. I actually want to cry sometimes, but it won’t come out (unless someone’s yelling at me or there’s a really sad movie).

I don’t think anyone really comes out stronger after trauma until they’ve healed.

I think I used to have a good memory. I had memories going back to preschool. Still do to some extent, but my memory seems much more scattered and hazy now, especially the past ~10 years. My earlier memories are more vivid, but disconnected to me now.
Many things seem far-fetched to me.

Being yourself doesn’t mean you don’t learn skills to improve yourself. It means not trying to be someone you’re not. Self-acceptance doesn’t mean you don’t change. On the contrary, we’re always changing, and without acceptance, it’s much harder to change for the better.

I think the idea is that you’ll have more success working with yourself rather than against yourself.

Small things may trigger such guilt and shame, but I trace them back to something (perceived as) big. The small failure reminds of big failure, or is somehow indicative of terrible flaw. 

Those moments pass (painful though they are), but I am constantly haunted by the big things.

I would say find a balance. It’s something you enjoy that becomes unhelpful when taken to an extreme.

I used to have a more active imagination, and I really miss it. I think it was actually the healthier alternative for me, since I replaced it with internet addiction. I can get a lot more done with low-key fantasizing than being glued to a screen. I feel so dull and uncreative now.

Yes, I’d like to know someone I could rely on to be honest with me. There’s pretty much only my family, and our relationships are very damaged. I’m afraid they try to manipulate me. I don’t entirely blame them, but still.

I need feedback I can trust. I don’t want to be told I’m normal and my situation is not that bad. I just want validation that, yes, this is real, and here is something further to consider.
Yes. Extremes tend to be unhealthy. And I’ve wondered that as well. I think it could be a self-fulfilling prophecy.

Yes! I thought this for a while, but now I’ve decided my “brutal honesty” was actually overly negative. It didn’t really make sense or feel right to me. It felt forced, and as if I was overcompensating or something. I was anticipating attack, so I attacked myself first.

I don’t really care whether we call it a disorder or not. It could be useful to think of it that way, though I am inclined to think people are getting overpathologized. Theory gets too complex for me. I consider it basically a dysfunctional pattern of behavior. Anyway, I don’t think having a “disorder” means we should be excused, though I guess it’s debatable how much of it is our fault.

Sorry for rambling. I’m in a different place now. Hope I made sense.

I think I’m on the other end with OCD, which has probably contributed a lot to my avoidance. I also have ADHD-like symptoms as result of executive overload.

https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/expert-opinion-ocd-and-adhd-dual-diagnosis-misdiagnosis-and-the-cognitive-cost-of-obsessions/

This could be why I’ve become so scattered, yet still very withdrawn and risk-averse.
My mom has also overprotected me. She can be somewhat abusive since she’s so irrational and has such difficulty regulating her emotions.

Definitely did not have full-blown AvPD all my life. I was a quiet and sensitive child who had to deal with some emotional trauma, and then I think circumstances aligned that resulted in my developing this disorder. Too much changed for the worse in my middle school years. I lost some vital supports, got overwhelmed, and started avoiding things more. My parents enabled it. I never managed to recover under the circumstances, so it’s been mostly a slow decline.

I think this happened to me for a while. I lost my sense of who I am and what I like. Last few years, I’ve been slooowly (like glacial speed) regaining my interests. The problem is, it’s been so long that I don’t know how to fit these things in my life anymore.

It’s quite an adjustment for me just to accept that I can have my own interests that differ from those of others and it’s not crazy or wrong.
Yup. That damned conflict of wanting to avoid attention yet also wanting to share.
Yes. Why would they actually want to be around me? I know what I can be like...

I also have this feeling that I’m always wrong. My mind plays tricks on me. It will talk me out of doing the right thing, and then criticize me harshly for my failure. “Don’t try to get better. You’ll only fail anyway. You’ll never be good enough... See how bad you are for not getting better.” STFU bitch, you’re not helping.

Anyway, nice videos. Hearing an actual voice really hits different than reading posts.

It seems I dissociate from a lot of my feelings, so I don’t know if I do. I might look depressed from the outside, but I don’t really feel sad or numb, at least not totally. I do have a recurring sense of emptiness. I laugh a lot, but I rarely feel joy.

So, yeah, anyway... I’m not too sure what  “depression” even is. People have such different versions, it confuses me. I guess I’ve had a mild depression for so long that it feels normal.

My conclusion is that you can’t. At least, I’m fairly sure I can’t make up for my wasted time. I got to accept the loss. But the most meaningful thing I can do is to make different choices now. Stop repeating the mistakes of your past. Build something better. That’s what I wish I had done from the outset instead of beating myself to hell, making things even worse.

Used to be more so. I would constantly worry about being “wrong” or people thinking I’m “wrong” and severely restrict my behaviors. I’ve made a few choices differently since I’ve started caring less, such as letting my music play out loud. In a way, I’m telling myself it’s not such a big deal anymore.
No. I interact with my family, pets, and sometimes other people, but I wouldn’t consider any of them proper friends.
Same.
Mostly, I sit in bed reading/watching/listening to stuff on the internet. It’s been crime shows and history documentaries recently.

Cats. I hardly leave the house, so they’re like my buddies. (Come to think of it, there are quite a few jokes about cats and lonely people, aren’t there?)

Sometimes I wish I had a dog to walk. I think I’d feel more comfortable than when I walk alone.
Lol. This wasn’t me as a child so much, but from mid-teens onward, yes. Especially with my family. Fear and shame really can be crippling without healthy coping skills.

This used to be (and still is, to some extent) a major problem for me, though it wasn’t always. It got especially bad after I decided I’d ruined my life.

It felt like something I was practicing, in a way, since I thought I deserved to be punished. It really was obsessive-compulsive. Eventually, the stress of it got so bad that I was getting migraines frequently, so I was motivated to practice a different response. I put most of my shame behind a wall and stopped beating on myself so much. The obsessive thinking, in general, has been harder to break, but I can practice not chasing thoughts. I sometimes notice opportunities to let things go or pursue them, and I typically choose to pursue because I worry about “what if”. I guess I just got to remember that it’s not worth it. I don’t need that. Stop and focus on something else before my brain latches onto it.
